description: Abstracted bass fills (chord functions, tick rhythm, note functions). See docs/research/phase8-fill-corpus.md for the schema and vocabulary. No tab or note-for-note transcription is reproduced; sources attest existence.

examples.title: Man in the Mirror (Michael Jackson): G -> Ab direct lift on 'change'
examples.note: Departing chord assumed V; T:5 = Eb (new key's 5), T-1 = G, the old tonic, which a +1 lift always provides.

examples.title: Love on Top (Beyonce): four successive +1 lifts C->Db->D->Eb->E, no pivot
examples.note: Melody reaches the new key at the pickup, before the band. Repeated lifts: register must not drift past the top of the range.

examples.title: Love on Top, last lift Eb -> E: same move after three earlier lifts
examples.note: Spelling check: the new key is E (sharps) after Eb (flats); T-1 must spell D#, not Eb.

examples.title: I Will Always Love You (Whitney Houston): A -> B into the final chorus

examples.note: A = new key's 5, C# = its 7; C# over G is a cross-relation with the old key's C, but on a weak 8th into the lift.

examples.title: A Lover's Concerto (The Toys): C -> Db prepared by Ab, the new key's V

examples.note: The 3 of Ab (C) is T-1 and the old tonic: a common tone of both keys and the leading tone.

examples.title: Hello, I Love You (The Doors): abrupt +1 with no preparation chord

examples.note: A is both the old V and the new IV; the move to E is a fifth down, D# (T-1) is the new leading tone.
